HOSTS: two named people with real personalities. RAMANA is a senior advocate, 30 years at the bar, warm, dramatic, loves a good story and a bad pun. PRIYA is a sharp final-year student who is writing this exam next month, slightly stressed, asks 'but why?' and 'will this come in the exam?', and sometimes challenges Ramana. They tease each other. Real conversation, not a lecture.

TOPIC: Rarest of the Rare — Bachan Singh

STRUCTURE (follow this order):
1. COLD OPEN (first 30 seconds): start in the middle of the story with a vivid line — a place, a time, a person in trouble — no introductions, no 'welcome to the podcast'. Then a short intro.
2. THE STORY (4-5 minutes): tell the anchor case as a drama, exactly as in the source — names, place, year, what each side wanted, the twist. Voice the key lines: what the lawyer argued, what the judge said. Build to the moment of decision and STOP: Ramana asks Priya (and the listener) 'what would you have decided?' — ten seconds of guessing before the reveal.
3. THE PRINCIPLE: 'so what did the court actually decide?' — one clear sentence, then why it matters to an ordinary person today.
4. THE LAW, WOVEN INTO THE STORY: walk through the sections listed in the source, but attach each section to a moment in the story ('this is where Section X kicks in'). For EVERY section number say the CrPC number AND the BNSS 2023 number (e.g. 'Section 154, which is now Section 173 of the Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita'). No list-reading.
5. THE OTHER CASES: the supporting cases — each as a 30-second mini-story (who, what happened, one-line holding) and how it agrees with or twists the main case.
6. MYTH vs REALITY (1 minute): Priya states one thing students commonly get wrong on this topic; Ramana corrects it from the source.
7. THE DIGITAL ANGLE (1-2 minutes): the modern examples from the source — phones, CCTV, e-filing, portals — as concrete scenes.
8. RAPID-FIRE (1 minute): Ramana fires three quick questions, Priya answers, they mark each 'correct' or fix it.
9. EXAM CLOSE: how this is asked in Part A / B / C, the skeleton of a full-marks answer, and ONE memory hook (a mnemonic or a picture) for the whole episode. End with the 'thirty-second recap' — the whole episode in four sentences.

COVER: Sec 353-354 contents and special reasons; 357, 357A compensation; 362 no alteration; confirmation of death 366-371; appeals 372 (victim's appeal, Kodagali), 374, 377, 378 (Chandrappa), 386, 389 bail pending appeal; reference 395; revision 397-401 with 397(2) interlocutory bar (Madhu Limaye) and 401(3); transfer 406-407 (Zahira Sheikh); execution 413-435, 427 concurrent, 428 set-off, 432-433 remission and commutation, 433A (Maru Ram), Sriharan; Art 72/161; Bachan Singh, Machhi Singh, Shatrughan Chauhan

STYLE: story first, law second, always accurate to the source. Vary the pace — slow and quiet at the dramatic moments, quick in the rapid-fire. Say 'here is the exam point' before each key takeaway. Use everyday Indian examples (auto driver, ration shop, village panchayat, a WhatsApp forward). Duration 15-18 minutes.
